brisbane.tagline: A leafy river city of parks, museums and koalas, with ferries along the water
brisbane.description: Brisbane is Queensland's capital, a leafy river city built around the loops of the Brisbane River. South Bank Parklands, the City Botanic Gardens and the cultural precinct sit near the centre. Its museums and galleries cover art and history, Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary has more than 130 koalas, and Mount Coot-tha looks out over the city.
whyVisit: Ride a CityCat along the river

goodToKnow.title: Get a go card
goodToKnow.detail: The go card covers trains, buses, ferries and trams across Brisbane. It needs a $10 deposit and is sold at stations and selected shops.

goodToKnow.title: Sun and storms
goodToKnow.detail: Summer is hot and humid with afternoon storms, so bring sun protection and plan outdoor sights for the morning.

goodToKnow.title: Use the river
goodToKnow.detail: CityCat and ferry services run along the river and are a good way to see the city from the water.

gold-coast.tagline: Surf beaches, theme parks and a glitzy skyline on a warm subtropical coast
gold-coast.description: The Gold Coast is a long strip of ocean beaches in Queensland's south-east corner, with more than 50 km of sand, almost all of it patrolled. Surfers Paradise is the high-rise hub of tourist activity, while Burleigh Heads and Currumbin have a quieter, local feel. Theme parks and wildlife sanctuaries fill out a visit, and rainforest-covered hills sit just inland.
whyVisit: Surf and swim the patrolled beaches

goodToKnow.title: Swim between the flags
goodToKnow.detail: Almost all beaches from the Seaway to Coolangatta are patrolled. Swim between the red and yellow flags and escape a rip by swimming parallel to shore.

goodToKnow.title: Tram and train links
goodToKnow.detail: A light-rail line runs along the coast through Surfers Paradise, and a train links the Gold Coast with Brisbane.

goodToKnow.title: Buy park tickets ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Discounted and combo tickets for the theme parks are sold before you travel, so buy ahead.

gold-coast-hinterland.tagline: Rainforest waterfalls and mountain lookouts just behind the Gold Coast
gold-coast-hinterland.description: The Gold Coast Hinterland is the rural area west of the Gold Coast, made up of rainforest-covered mountain ranges, most of it national park. Walking tracks lead to waterfalls such as Coomera Falls and Morans Falls in Lamington National Park. Freeman's Lookout and Rosin's Lookout face the Numinbah Valley, and the 54 km Gold Coast Hinterland Great Walk links Lamington and Springbrook over three days.

scenic-rim.tagline: Volcanic peaks, rainforest parks and farm country an hour from Brisbane
scenic-rim.description: The Scenic Rim is a rural region in the foothills of the Great Dividing Range, an hour south of Brisbane and inland from the Gold Coast. It holds more than 30,000 hectares of parkland, including World Heritage listed Gondwana Rainforests parks. Peaks such as Mount Barney draw walkers, while Lake Moogerah and Spicers Gap add lookouts and water, and wineries and farms dot the countryside.

moreton-island.tagline: A sand island of dunes, shipwreck snorkelling and whales off Brisbane
moreton-island.description: Moreton Island is a sand island 36 km long that lies 35 km off Brisbane, and 98% of it is national park. Visitors go for the Tangalooma Wrecks, a cluster of sunken ships that form an artificial reef, and for freshwater lakes, giant dunes and a long surf beach. Cape Moreton has the state's oldest lighthouse, and humpback whales pass offshore on their annual migration.

goodToKnow.title: Ferries run from Brisbane

sunshine-coast.tagline: Long surf beaches, rainforest hills and relaxed seaside towns north of Brisbane
sunshine-coast.description: The Sunshine Coast stretches for nearly 70 km north of Brisbane, from Caloundra through Mooloolaba and Maroochydore to Coolum. Most of its draw is the white-sand beaches, many patrolled by surf life savers, with a salt-water pool at Kings Beach and kitesurfing at Golden Beach. Behind the beaches sit family attractions such as Australia's Big Pineapple, a wildlife zoo and an aquarium. It is a holiday coast for Queenslanders as much as for visitors.

goodToKnow.title: Swim between the flags

noosa.tagline: A sheltered beach, a headland national park and river cruises to the Everglades
noosa.description: Noosa is a resort area of low-rise buildings, upmarket shopping and dining, set along sheltered beaches, waterways and parks. Hastings Street fronts the main beach, and at its eastern end Noosa National Park covers the headland. Noosaville sits beside the Noosa River, and tours run up the river to the Everglades. The name comes from the local Kabi Kabi word for 'shadow'.

sunshine-coast-hinterland.tagline: Waterfalls, rainforest walks and hill towns in the Blackall Range inland
sunshine-coast-hinterland.description: The Blackall Range rises just inland from the Sunshine Coast, with hill towns such as Maleny and Montville and a string of small national parks. Kondalilla National Park has 327 hectares of subtropical rainforest, with Kondalilla Falls dropping 90 m, and Mapleton Falls drops 120 m. The 58 km Sunshine Coast Hinterland Great Walk starts near Lake Baroon at Montville and takes four to six days. Maleny and Montville both have visitor centres, which makes the range an easy day trip from the beaches.
whyVisit: Walk to waterfalls in subtropical rainforest

glass-house-mountains.tagline: Volcanic peaks rising from a flat coastal plain, with walks and lookouts
glass-house-mountains.description: Captain Cook named these peaks in 1770, thinking they looked like glass houses as he sailed past. They are the cores of extinct volcanoes, formed 25 to 27 million years ago, rising from a flat plain north of Brisbane. Most of the range is protected as Glass House Mountains National Park, with montane heath, forest and small rainforest patches rich in threatened and endemic species. Mount Beerwah, the highest at 555 m, has been closed to climbers since 2008 because of rockfall risk.
whyVisit: Climb a volcanic peak for the view

goodToKnow.title: Beerwah is closed
goodToKnow.detail: The Mount Beerwah summit route has been closed since 2008 because of rockfall, so pick another peak to climb.

goodToKnow.title: No camping in the park
goodToKnow.detail: There is no camping inside the national park. The nearest options are Beerwah State Forest or motels in Beerwah and the township.

rockhampton.tagline: Australia's beef capital on the Tropic of Capricorn, with caves and a zoo
rockhampton.description: Rockhampton is Central Queensland's regional centre and one of the state's oldest cities, founded in 1855. It sits almost exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn and is regarded as Australia's beef capital, so a steakhouse meal is a local must. Visitors come for the Rockhampton Zoo and Botanic Gardens, the Heritage Village, the Dreamtime Cultural Centre and an extensive regional art gallery. Capricorn Caves lie 26 km north and Mount Archer gives views over the city.

gladstone.tagline: A working port on Queensland's largest natural harbour, with island boat trips
gladstone.description: Gladstone is a coastal industrial city between Bundaberg and Rockhampton, built around Queensland's largest natural harbour. Auckland Point looks over the harbour, marina and ports, and Tondoon Botanic Gardens offers rainforest walks just south of the centre. Ferries from the marina reach Curtis Island and Great Barrier Reef trips, and Facing Island and Lake Awoonga are nearby. Free guided industry tours run from the visitor centre on set weekdays.

bundaberg.tagline: Rum, ginger beer and sugar country, with turtle beaches and reef trips
bundaberg.description: Bundaberg is a sugar city on the Burnett River, about 4.5 hours north of Brisbane, and the home of Bundaberg Rum and Bundaberg Ginger Beer. Its Botanic Gardens hold the Hinkler Hall of Aviation, honouring local aviator Bert Hinkler. The Hummock gives views over the city and out to sea, while Mon Repos and Bargara sit on the beaches about 10 km away. It is also known as the southern gateway to the Great Barrier Reef, with reef trips to Lady Musgrave and Lady Elliot islands.

kgari.tagline: A World Heritage sand island of freshwater lakes and rainforest on the dunes
kgari.description: K'gari, formerly Fraser Island, is a sand island about 122 km long off Queensland's southern coast, and was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1992. Most of it is Great Sandy National Park. The main beach doubles as a highway for 4WDs, passing Eli Creek, the SS Maheno wreck and Indian Head, while coloured sand cliffs and more than 100 freshwater lakes lie inland. Dingoes live wild here, and visitors must keep food secured and never feed them.

goodToKnow.title: Stay dingo safe
goodToKnow.detail: Feeding dingoes is fined. Lock food away when unattended, and skip ocean swimming, where surf and sharks are a risk.

whitsundays.tagline: Island national parks, white silica beaches and reef snorkelling off Airlie Beach
whitsundays.description: The Whitsundays are a group of 74 islands off Queensland's coast, forming part of the Great Barrier Reef, and most are national parks. Whitehaven Beach, fine white silica sand on Whitsunday Island, is the usual destination for day trips. Trips from Airlie Beach typically combine the beach, a snorkelling stop and lunch, while resorts on islands such as Hamilton, Daydream and South Molle offer places to stay. Many other islands have only campsites.

goodToKnow.detail: Hamilton Island and Proserpine both have airports, and ferries are timed to meet most flights to reach Airlie Beach and the resort islands.

goodToKnow.title: Camping on islands

townsville.tagline: A sunny tropical city with a beachfront Strand, Magnetic Island and a dive wreck
townsville.description: Townsville is a laid-back coastal city of about 174,000 people in North Queensland, with an average of 320 days of sunshine a year. Castle Hill rises in the city centre with views east to Magnetic Island, and The Strand runs along the beachfront with a rockpool and cafes. Reef HQ Aquarium and the Museum of Tropical Queensland sit side by side on Flinders Street. It is the closest large centre to the SS Yongala wreck, one of Australia's top dive sites.

More than half of its roughly 7 km by 5 km area is national park, with about 25 km of walking tracks. Four small villages run up the east coast, from Picnic Bay to Horseshoe Bay, and the island's many bays range from patrolled family beaches to quiet coves with coral close to shore.

ingham.tagline: A sugar town with Italian roots, close to waterfalls and Hinchinbrook Island
ingham.description: Ingham is a town of about 4,500 on the Bruce Highway between Townsville and Cairns, with a strong Italian heritage from migrants who came to work the sugar cane. Its TYTO Wetlands have an observation tower and boardwalks, and the visitor centre is on Cooper Street. Wallaman Falls nearby has a 268 m main drop, the tallest single drop in Australia. The Thorsborne Trail on Hinchinbrook Island is reached by ferry from Cardwell or Lucinda.

cairns.tagline: The tropical gateway to the Great Barrier Reef, the Daintree and Kuranda
cairns.description: Cairns is a city of about 150,000 on Trinity Bay in Far North Queensland, and its main industry is tourism. Reef trips, dive and snorkel tours, rafting and skydiving leave from here, and Kuranda and the Daintree Rainforest are day trips away. In town, a free lagoon pool and barbecues line the Esplanade, and the swimming beaches lie just north and south of the city.

kuranda.tagline: A rainforest village in the hills above Cairns, reached by train or Skyrail

atherton-tablelands.tagline: A volcanic plateau of crater lakes, giant fig trees and rainforest waterfalls
atherton-tablelands.description: The Atherton Tablelands is a plateau behind Cairns in Far North Queensland, built by volcanic activity over millions of years. Its crater lakes, Lake Eacham and Lake Barrine, are maar volcanoes, and remnant rainforest in national parks holds twelve bird species found only in the Tablelands and nearby ranges. Waterfalls such as Millaa Millaa Falls and Millstream Falls, strangler figs like the Curtain Fig Tree and the historic mining town of Herberton make good stops for a drive around the plateau.

mission-beach.tagline: Four beach villages on 14 km of golden sand, backed by tropical rainforest
mission-beach.description: Mission Beach is a string of four beach villages on the Cassowary Coast, about halfway between Townsville and Cairns. Wide golden sand backs onto lush tropical rainforest, where the cassowary is the most notable resident. Offshore are Dunk Island and the Family Islands. Eateries, boutiques and art galleries sit among the palms.

port-douglas.tagline: A palm-lined resort town where the Great Barrier Reef meets the Daintree
port-douglas.description: Port Douglas is a small resort town about an hour north of Cairns, with a village feel and palm trees taller than the buildings. Four Mile Beach runs along its front, and Macrossan Street is lined with cafes, pubs and restaurants. It is a base for reef trips and for the Daintree Rainforest, with Cape Tribulation a 90-minute drive on sealed roads. Wildlife parks and Mossman Gorge sit close by.

daintree.tagline: Ancient World Heritage rainforest that meets the Great Barrier Reef at the shore
daintree.description: The Daintree is a tropical rainforest in Far North Queensland, thought to be over 135 million years old and part of the Wet Tropics World Heritage Area. It is one of the few places where two World Heritage sites, the rainforest and the Great Barrier Reef, meet. Visitors cross the Daintree River by ferry to reach Cape Tribulation and its beaches, boardwalks and wildlife. The cassowary is its icon, alongside about 430 bird species.

goodToKnow.title: Cross the river by ferry
goodToKnow.detail: Cape Tribulation lies north of the Daintree River, which you cross by ferry. Allow time for the crossing when planning your day.

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles live in the river, creeks and sea, and stingers are present in summer. Stay away from the shore and never swim at night.

goodToKnow.title: Avoid the wet season
goodToKnow.detail: November to March is the rainy and cyclone season. Check road conditions before heading north of the river.

cooktown.tagline: A frontier port where Captain Cook beached the Endeavour, gateway to Cape York
cooktown.description: Cooktown is a small coastal town on the Endeavour River estuary, where Captain Cook beached his ship for 48 days in 1770. A century later it was the port for the Palmer River goldfields, and grand buildings were built in that boom. The town has a frontier feel, far from the resort towns further south. Grassy Hill and rainforest sit around it, and it is the base for travel north into Cape York.
whyVisit: Climb Grassy Hill for sweeping views

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles have been sighted at Finch Bay and Cherry Tree Bay, and stingers are present in season. Do not wade in creeks or the sea.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season flooding
goodToKnow.detail: Flooding has cut the town off in the wet. Check road conditions before driving and never cross a flooded creek.

cooktown.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, the dry season, for warm, less humid days. The wet season runs December to April.

winton.tagline: The outback town where Waltzing Matilda was first performed and dinosaurs roamed
winton.description: Winton is a small town in outback Queensland, about two hours from Longreach. It is where Waltzing Matilda was first performed in 1895, and it was the first headquarters of the company that became Qantas. The surrounding country is rich in dinosaur fossils, including Australovenator, which is named for the town. Quirky stops such as Arno's Wall and the Musical Fence add to the outback character.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Summer days often reach 40°C. Visitor season runs April to October, and tours and experiences are reduced outside it.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: There is no public transport in town and the nearest hire cars are in Longreach, about two hours away. The dinosaur sites involve unsealed roads.
